claims.text: UN 242 Palestinian journalists killed as of 11 Aug 2025; CPJ 192 (10 Aug 2025), later removed names it found engaged in combat (22, then 20 in June 2026, 19 in Sept 2026); IFJ removed 8 and added 14 in July 2026, raising its count from 235 to 241; RSF: Israel biggest killer of journalists in 2025; CPJ: 2025 deadliest year in its records, Israel responsible for two-thirds of press killings 2024 and 2025.

Israel says some journalists were militants; IDF named Anas al-Sharif (killed 10 Aug 2025) a Hamas operative, rejected by Al Jazeera and CPJ; Hamza Dahdouh (7 Jan 2024): IDF changed its account, Washington Post found no indication he was doing anything but journalism; RSF: 'Journalists are not terrorists'; +972 reported a 'Legitimization Cell'; Nasser hospital double strike 25 Aug 2025 killed at least 20 incl. 5 journalists; Netanyahu's office 'deeply regrets'.

CPJ: 129 journalists and media workers killed worldwide in 2025, a record since 1992; Israel responsible for about two-thirds, mostly Palestinian journalists in Gaza; 47 'murders' (targeted killings) in 2025, the most in a decade; 28 drone cases by Israel's military in Gaza; Ginsberg: 'Journalists are being killed in record numbers at a time when access to information is more important than ever'.

July 2025: AFP asked Israel to evacuate its freelance journalists, saying their situation was 'untenable'; AFP's Society of Journalists: 'We fear learning of their deaths at any moment'; photographer Bashar said his 'body is thin'; Al Jazeera cited forced starvation.

Wael Dahdouh's wife, son, daughter and grandson killed in Oct 2023 Nuseirat strike; he was injured in Dec 2023 drone strike that killed his cameraman; son Hamza and Mustafa Thuraya killed in a strike on their car; IDF: struck 'a terrorist who operated an aircraft that posed a threat'; Al Jazeera: they were not flying a drone; Dahdouh: 'We are going to proceed as long as we are alive and breathing.'
